title: Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: multi-tool parallelism, result injection, and retries
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers are building flows that call multiple tools in parallel (search, run, fetch) and need deterministic, low-latency injection of tool outputs back into the model context. We observed: 1) non-deterministic insertion ordering when parallel calls finish at different times; 2) poor UX when a transient tool failure causes the whole request to abort; 3) streaming instability when partial tool results arrive mid-stream. This PR: - Adds a tool execution orchestration layer that supports concurrent tool invocation with configurable concurrency and deterministic ordering options. - Implements a per-tool retry policy with exponential backoff, jitter, and idempotency key handling. - Introduces explicit tool-result injection points into the execution plan so tool outputs are merged into model prompts in a controlled, checkpointed manner. - Improves streaming stability by buffering tool-result patches and sending checkpointed deltas to the stream consumer; adds a graceful degradation path that inserts a standardized tool-error fragment instead of failing the entire generation. - Updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to expose tool invocation metadata in responses (tool_calls array + tool_call.status) and to accept an extended tool spec in requests for compatibility with common open-source toolchains. - Adds metrics (tool_latency_ms, tool_retries_total, tool_injection_lag_ms) and new e2e tests covering multi-tool parallel flows and retry scenarios. A checklist: - [x] Orchestration layer implementation - [x] Retry/backoff + idempotency support - [x] Streaming checkpoint buffering - [x] OpenAI-compat response changes + docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Release notes

Notes on behaviour: - Default behaviour is best-effort fast injection: tools are invoked in parallel and the first available result is injected into its planned slot; if deterministic ordering is requested (via execution config), the orchestrator waits for all required tool results up to a configurable timeout and injects in the declared order. - Retry semantics are opt-in per-tool; by default a single retry with short backoff is attempted for network-level errors; persistent failures produce a standard tool-error injection object that the model can see and react to. - Streaming: we checkpoint at tool-insertion boundaries so partial text consumed by downstream model is coherent; if an in-flight tool result arrives while the stream is active we send a compact patch message followed by a stable continuation token. - Backwards compatibility: existing non-tool workflows are unchanged. OpenAI-compat clients will see an opt-in response field `tool_calls` and opt-in request flags.

Risk and mitigation: this touches runtime execution and streaming code paths; mitigations include extensive unit tests, a canary rollout flag, and a toggle to disable deterministic waiting in production if latency regressions are observed.
commits: feat(tool-exec): add orchestrator for parallel tool invocation and deterministic injection
fix(tool-exec): implement idempotency keys and safer retry handling
perf(streaming): checkpointed buffer for tool-result patches to stabilize streams
feat(openai-compat): include tool_calls metadata in responses and accept extended tool specs
test: add unit + e2e tests for multi-tool parallel flows and retry scenarios
docs: document tool-calling execution config and OpenAI-compat changes
ci: add canary pipeline for tool-calling e2e tests
discussion:
Lena: Can you clarify the default concurrency?
Aisha: Default concurrency is 4 for tool invocation; it's configurable per-execution and per-deployment.
Kofi: What about ordered injection causing latency spikes?
Aisha: Deterministic ordering is opt-in and has a configurable wait timeout. We added a canary flag so we can monitor impact before enabling.
Evan: Is the tool-error injection schema stable? Will clients parse it?
Aisha: We defined a compact, versioned `tool_error` fragment in the OpenAI-compat response; docs include examples and migration guidance.
Lena: CI flaky test on first run — looks like timeouts in e2e.
Aisha: I increased the test timeouts and added retry logic to the CI job; reran and green.
Kofi: Suggest adding one more metric for 'tool_queue_depth'
Aisha: Added metric+dashboard in observability files.
Reviewer approvals: Lena approved after changes; Kofi requested a small refactor to make backoff strategy pluggable (addressed); Evan approved.
release_notes: Added parallel multi-tool invocation with configurable concurrency and deterministic injection options; per-tool retry policies and idempotency handling; streaming checkpointing for stable tool-result patches; OpenAI-compat extension to expose tool_calls metadata; new observability metrics for tool latency and retries.
